text: After this you can explain the proposed path from a bid request to a committed result.

Proposed network rules give each room one trusted authority for bid decisions. The authority validates roles, timing, price, lot and accepted sequence before changing state. The service rejects retransmissions rather than recording another purchase. Rejoining participants receive committed history rather than relying on their last displayed screen.

items: Send a bid request with the current lot and room revision. You should see: A request tied to a specific auction state. If not: Refresh when the room has moved on.
Check bidder authority and the live auction conditions. You should see: A valid request or an explicit rejection reason. If not: Keep the previous committed result unchanged.
Record an accepted bid once and publish the new state. You should see: One shared outcome for every connected participant. If not: Reconcile the authoritative log before retrying.
Inferred: Two devices send an offer at nearly the same time. The room authority records only the winning valid transition.

text: One room authority decides; screens display the result.
A browser display is not itself proof that a bid was accepted.

items: Trusting a local screen to enforce prices. A changed or delayed client can send invalid information. Fix: Validate on the authoritative service.
